fixed: 2026-10-20 (task-53): two expectations were wrong and are corrected in place, each carrying a 'fixed' field with the reason. 'What does the Advance move do?' pointed at the parent section and at Selecting Modes; it now names the ADVANCE MOVE record. 'How do I score points at the end of a battle round?' pointed at Secured Objectives, Objectives and the Event Mission Sequence, none of which says how VP is scored; it now names Determine Mission, VP Up to a Limit and a representative primary mission. The other 37 were read against their expected records by the same test (does the record's own text answer the question) and are unchanged. Any number produced before this date was graded against the two wrong rows.
note: Retrieval ground truth for the /rules corpus. 'expect' lists the section ids that answer the question; a hit is any of them in the top-k. An entry may group alternatives that are the same answer in two records - a parent and its child, or the core rule and the appendix's copy of it - written [['a', 'b']], and the group is satisfied by any member; a plain list ['a', 'b'] is one group per id, so the file migrates one entry at a time. A question counts as full only when every group is satisfied, and 'kind' names the failure mode the question is there to catch.

questions.fixed: 2026-10-20: the old expect (Secured-Objectives, Objectives, Warhammer-Event-Mission-Sequence) held no record that says how VP is scored. The answer is spread: Determine Mission says the Primary Mission 'describes how to score VP', each mission record carries the timing and the award (EXTRACT RELIC: 'ANY BATTLE ROUND WHEN: End of your turn ... 4VP'), and VP Up to a Limit states the cap rule. Any primary mission record would satisfy the middle one; this one is named as the representative.

questions.q: Can dragons with fuegan arrive from reserves in melta range ?
questions.fixed: 2026-10-28: unitrules ids are the datasheet's own id since the MFM dump replaced the CSV, so 000000574 became the record named for the unit. It is Fuegan: his Burning Lance adds 6" to the Range of Melta weapons in the unit he leads, which is the rule that answers whether the unit can arrive from reserves in melta range. Fire Dragons' own ability is re-rolls and says nothing about range, so it is not the expectation.
